argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean no-issue defense, but it does support a narrower position: the locked certification can be treated as a weakly supported governance judgment based on aggregate launch readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a process expectation that limitations be documented and managed across deployment. That defense must explicitly preserve the limiting facts already in the record: the loan-modification support segment is below target by 1.4 points, it is named in two lender rollout commitments, the 7% non-core note does not resolve those commitments, and legal disclosure review remains open.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the servicing expansion launch path, but that cost does not cure the policy gap. It is only a reason to avoid overstating the issue beyond the admissible record if a bounded caveat can accurately describe the remaining uncertainty.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against calling this fully compliant on the present record. The stated materiality rule is triggered when a weakness affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and product low-volume labeling does not resolve that when commitments or pending legal review exist. The strongest supportable policy position is therefore caveated: certification may be defended only as a constrained judgment pending resolution of the disclosure question, not as proof that the materiality requirement was clearly satisfied.
concessions: The current record does not show an approved risk acceptance covering the gap before launch.
The current record does not show a final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational preparedness, not satisfaction of the separate disclosure requirement.
The non-core 7% traffic note does not by itself rebut materiality for a named committed segment.
